narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated an 80% probability that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. That is a high-risk estimate, not a certainty, but it was strong enough to drive the admission decision.

The most influential factor was your third-year class position: you were recorded in the first decile, while accepted students averaged near the sixth decile, and this pushed the prediction toward failure. Your first-year class position was the second most influential factor; it was also in the first decile versus an accepted-student average near the sixth, and it likewise pushed toward failure. Your LSAT score of 42 was the third most important factor. It was above the accepted-student average of about 37 and pushed toward passing, but it was not enough to offset the two earlier academic-position signals.

To strengthen a future application, meet with an academic advisor to understand and address what drove your early class standing, consider additional coursework or a post-baccalaureate record that demonstrates consistent readiness, and prepare a concise explanation of your academic trajectory. Reapplying after showing improved performance, or applying to programs with a better fit, may be more productive than reapplying immediately with the same record.
